payload.name: Detail-Level Coverage Check Before Skip
payload.description: When deciding whether to SKIP or MERGE a candidate during construction, check whether the existing memory explicitly contains every distinct fact in the candidate; apply before any SKIP or MERGE.
content: During CRUD decisions, before SKIPping or MERGEing a candidate, verify the target memory explicitly contains every distinct factual detail in the candidate (who, what, when, and any specific artifact or event).
If any detail is missing, do not SKIP or MERGE; add the candidate as a new memory or enrich the existing memory with the missing details.
Do not treat a broader thematic statement (e.g., 'writing brought comfort to others') as covering a specific distinct fact (e.g., 'someone wrote her a letter about her blog post on a hard moment').
Stop after preserving the missing details; do not rewrite or duplicate unrelated existing content.

solves: Construction agents sometimes discard a correctly extracted event candidate because an existing memory covers the same subject or a related outcome, but the existing memory omits a specific factual detail. This skill prevents loss of answerable facts by requiring a detail-level coverage check before SKIP/MERGE decisions.
